spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** In traditional releases, rolling back a buggy feature requires a git revert, CI build, and container redeployment—taking 15–45 minutes while errors spike.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Feature Flag Progressive Rollout & Kill-Switch State Machine (DARK (0%) -> CANARY (1–10%) -> GA (100%)); SSE Rule Streaming + Sub-Millisecond In-Memory Evaluation (Flag Control Plane -> SSE / CDN Edge -> Pod In-Memory SDK -> Hardcoded Fallback).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Feature flags complement—rather than replace—Kubernetes/ALB canary traffic splitting. A production feature-flag platform separates the **Control Plane** (audit-logged rule editor + SSE/CDN rule distribution) from **Data-Plane Evaluation** (in-memory SDKs inside each pod with hardcoded fallback defaults).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how progressive rollouts, canary evaluation, and graceful degradation work together in production.

learningJourney.title: What are Feature Flags
learningJourney.explanation:
In traditional releases, rolling back a buggy feature requires a git revert, CI build, and container redeployment—taking 15–45 minutes while errors spike. **Feature flags** (LaunchDarkly, Unleash, OpenFeature) separate **deployment** (pushing binaries to production) from **release** (exposing behavior to users).

Engineers merge incomplete work behind a flag defaulting to `false` (dark launch). SDKs stream rule updates via SSE/WebSockets into an in-memory cache and evaluate `(flagKey + userId) % 100` locally in `<50 µs`—never making a per-request network call.

learningJourney.title: Why Trunk-Based Teams Need Decoupled Releases
learningJourney.explanation: Long-lived feature branches cause painful merge conflicts and big-bang releases. Feature flags let teams merge daily to `main` while controlling blast radius in production: start with `dark-shadow` traffic, ramp to 1% internal users, and flip an instant kill switch if p99 latency degrades.

benefits: Gradually shifts 1% -> 10% -> 100% of queries from Elasticsearch to OpenSearch with instant fallback.

benefits: Disables non-critical GPU/ML recommendations in <1s during 12x flash-sale traffic surges.
costs: Fallback path (e.g., cached trending items) must be tested in CI so it doesn't crash when flipped.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Static Environment Config (DB URLs, Ports)
benefits: Environment variables or Kubernetes ConfigMaps are simpler and audited at deploy time.
costs: Wrapping static infra bindings in runtime flags adds unnecessary SDK state and complexity.

learningJourney.title: Local Deterministic Bucketing & Safe Fallback Defaults
learningJourney.explanation: Production flag evaluation must be **O(1) in-memory**, **deterministic** across pods, and **safe on failure**. Never reuse old flag keys (which caused Knight Capital's $440M outage), and always test both `true` and `false` branches in CI.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```python
import hashlib

def evaluate_percentage_flag(flag_key: str, user_id: str, rollout_pct: int, default: bool = False) -> bool:
    if not flag_key or not user_id:
        return default
    if rollout_pct <= 0:
        return False
    if rollout_pct >= 100:
        return True
    # Deterministic sticky bucketing across all stateless pods
    digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{flag_key}:{user_id}".encode("utf-8")).digest()
    bucket = int.from_bytes(digest[:4], "big") % 100
    return bucket < rollout_pct
```

learningJourney.explanation: Feature flags complement—rather than replace—Kubernetes/ALB canary traffic splitting.

benefits: <0.1 ms local evaluation; targeting rules and PII never leave your backend.
costs: Stale flags accumulate `2^N` code paths unless pruned via automated expiration alerts.

benefits: Evaluates cohort before hitting origin, enabling full-page CDN cache segmentation.
costs: Limited payload size and harder to access deep backend user entitlements.

benefits: Zero flag code in the app; isolates process-level crashes or memory leaks.
costs: Cannot toggle per-tenant entitlements or individual sub-features inside a single request.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why do production feature-flag SDKs stream rulesets into local pod memory rather than calling the feature-flag API on every incoming HTTP request?

options.text: To keep flag evaluation under ~50 microseconds and prevent control-plane outages from taking down request serving
options.feedback: Correct: local evaluation eliminates per-request network latency and ensures the service survives control-plane outages.

options.text: Because HTTP APIs cannot evaluate MurmurHash3 or SHA-256
options.feedback: Remote APIs can hash, but the network RTT and single-point-of-failure dependency are unacceptable on hot paths.

options.text: So that different pods can assign the same user to different canary cohorts
options.feedback: Deterministic hashing guarantees all pods assign the same user to the exact same cohort.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
